The part nobody films

More projects shouldn’t mean more nights in Premiere Pro.

  1. 01

    The backlog

    A wedding, a conference, two brand videos — all still sitting on a drive. Every new project quietly adds one more to the pile.

  2. 02

    The client who keeps asking

    “Any news on the video?” A couple, an event organiser, a brand manager. You reply with another date — and hope you can keep it this time.

  3. 03

    Hours before the first cut

    Culling, syncing audio, lining up multicam, labelling clips. Whole evenings gone before you make a single creative decision.

  4. 04

    No room for the next yes

    A new enquiry lands — a wedding, an event, a campaign. You’re free to shoot it, yet you hesitate, because you know who will be editing it.

You started filming for the moments. Not for the export queue.

How it works

From footage → finished film.

Five stages between your memory card and the moment your client presses play.

  1. You send the cards — every angle, every take, every audio file, exactly as the day left them.

  2. We select, sync and shape the story: the moments that matter, in the order that makes people feel something.

  3. Your grade, shot by shot. Skin that looks like skin, light that looks the way the day felt.

  4. Voices, ambience and music — cleaned and balanced so nothing pulls the viewer out of the moment.

  5. The film, the teaser, the reels — every format you need, ready to send under your name.

Your style, not ours

We don’t impose our style. We learn yours.

Every studio has a signature — how you open a film, the music you’d never use, how long you hold on a face. Before we touch your footage, we write it down.

  1. 01

    Two or three reference films

    Send the films you’re proudest of. They become our brief.

  2. 02

    Your style guide and presets

    Grade, music, pacing and story rules — documented, and built into presets we use on every project.

  3. 03

    A feedback loop that sticks

    Every note you give goes back into the guide, so each new edit needs fewer.

FAQ

Before you ask.

The questions every studio asks before sending the first project.

How long does an edit take?

We agree a delivery date for every project before we start. As a guide: two to three weeks for a wedding highlight, three to five days for reels and short content.

How many revisions are included?

Two rounds of notes on every cut. Notes are timecoded and kept in one place, so nothing gets lost.

How do I send the footage?

Upload it straight from the cards in your client panel. No renaming or sorting needed.

Which software do you edit in? Do I get the project files?

Premiere Pro for the edit, DaVinci Resolve for color. If you want the project files to finish something yourself, just ask.

Who handles music licensing?

You choose the music, or tell us which library you license from, and we cut to it.

Is my footage safe? Will you sign an NDA?

We sign an NDA with every studio. Footage is stored on encrypted drives and deleted 90 days after final delivery.

What if I don’t like the first edit?

That’s exactly what the first project is for. Your notes go straight into the style guide, and we refine until the edit feels like yours.

Can I send weddings, events and content?

Yes. Every level covers all three, mixed however your year needs.
